# Turkish flag

Models drawing the crescent and star from memory get it almost right: the inner circle is shifted, the star is too big or turned, the red changes every time. Almost right is wrong for a national flag. Never draw these shapes by hand. Copy the vector below and only scale or move it as one piece.

## The vector

Coordinates are in units where the flag's width (hoist height) G = 60000. The flag spans x 0 to 90000 and y -30000 to 30000, so its centre line is y = 0.

```svg
<!-- crescent -->
<path d="M42675 8021a15000 15000 0 1 1 0-16042 12000 12000 0 1 0 0 16042z"/>
<!-- star -->
<path d="M41750 0l13568-4408-8386 11541V-7133l8386 11541z"/>
```

Full flag: [assets/flag-of-turkey.svg](assets/flag-of-turkey.svg). It leaves out the white hem, for screen use. Crescent and star only, tightly cropped, white on transparent, so place it on red: [assets/crescent-and-star.svg](assets/crescent-and-star.svg).

Colours on screen: red `#DC0D15`, white `#FFFFFF`. This red is a convention, not the flag's legal colour. I found no government source that defines a screen colour for the flag. `#DC0D15` is the main red in the [Interior Ministry's current identity guide](https://www.icisleri.gov.tr/kurumsal-kimlik-kilavuz), and the ministry says its logo uses flag red. The legal red is a set of cloth coordinates in the regulation; see [references/construction.md](references/construction.md#colour).

These paths are computed from the official construction table attached to Law No. 2893 (Türk Bayrağı Kanunu, 1983), reproduced in [references/construction.md](references/construction.md). A Turkish and English diagram is in [references/construction-sheet.svg](references/construction-sheet.svg), and every value is in [references/construction.json](references/construction.json) for tools. Check any change against the table. The star's position follows E = G/3, which is a judgement: the official texts have a small conflict, explained in the construction notes.

## Putting it somewhere else

To place the crescent and star on a shield, badge, button or icon, wrap both paths in one group and use one transform:

```svg
<g fill="#fff" transform="translate(CX CY) scale(S) translate(-35159 0)">
  <path d="M42675 8021a15000 15000 0 1 1 0-16042 12000 12000 0 1 0 0 16042z"/>
  <path d="M41750 0l13568-4408-8386 11541V-7133l8386 11541z"/>
</g>
```

- `35159 0` is the centre of the emblem's bounding box (x 15000 to 55318, y -15000 to 15000), so `CX CY` is where its centre lands.
- `S = targetWidth / 40318`. Example: 300 px wide means `S = 0.00744`.
- Use the same scale on both axes. Never stretch.
- This template centres the emblem on a point. Don't use it to place the emblem on a whole flag; use the flag asset, where the emblem isn't centred.
- Keep it at least 24 px wide. At 12 px the star turns into a blob and the crescent's tips disappear.

## Rules

1. Copy the path data exactly. Don't round, simplify, re-type or redraw it, and don't rebuild it from `<circle>` elements and a star polygon unless you check every number against the construction sheet.
2. Move, scale and rotate the crescent and star together, never one alone. Their positions come from the law's table. An animation may move them, as long as it ends with both in place.
3. The star has one point aimed straight at the crescent (pointing to the hoist). Don't turn it.
4. The crescent opens toward the fly (away from the pole). If the design is mirrored for a right-to-left layout, still don't mirror the flag.
5. Fill only. No `stroke` on the white shapes: a stroke, especially with `stroke-linejoin="round"`, rounds the star's tips and fattens the crescent.
6. Keep the default `fill-rule` (nonzero). The star path crosses itself, and `fill-rule="evenodd"` punches a pentagon hole in its middle.
7. Use `#DC0D15` on screens. Not `red`, `#FF0000` or another brand's red. Use the regulation's coordinates for cloth.
8. A whole flag is 3:2 (length 1.5 G). Don't crop or stretch it to fit a square. Put it in a 3:2 box or use the crescent and star alone.

## Animating it

- The final frame has to be the exact static vector, with no leftover stroke, dash, scale or rotation.
- Reveal shapes with a mask (a sweep, a wipe, a growing circle) instead of drawing outlines with `stroke-dashoffset`. Outline drawing leaves a seam where the dash ends.
- To animate the star, scale or rotate it around its own centre `(49250, 0)` and end at scale 1, rotation 0.
- Leave room for any overshoot: the example's star grows about 15% mid-animation, so a tightly cropped viewBox clips it.
- Give each copy of the example its own mask `id`. Two copies with the same id can break the sweep.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by showing the static vector. SVG animation can't do this alone, so check it in code and pick which version to render.
- Renderers without SMIL support won't show this correctly, so use the static vector there too.

Example: crescent sweeps in, then the star spins into place, ending on the exact shape:

```svg
<defs>
  <mask id="sweep" maskUnits="userSpaceOnUse" x="14000" y="-16000" width="32000" height="32000">
    <circle cx="30000" cy="0" r="7600" fill="none" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="15200"
      pathLength="1" stroke-dasharray="1" stroke-dashoffset="1">
      <animate attributeName="stroke-dashoffset" values="1;0" dur="0.9s" fill="freeze"/>
    </circle>
  </mask>
</defs>
<g fill="#fff" transform="translate(CX CY) scale(S) translate(-35159 0)">
  <path mask="url(#sweep)" d="M42675 8021a15000 15000 0 1 1 0-16042 12000 12000 0 1 0 0 16042z">
    <set attributeName="mask" to="none" begin="0.9s" fill="freeze"/>
  </path>
  <g transform="translate(49250 0)">
    <g transform="scale(0)">
      <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="scale" values="0;1.15;1" keyTimes="0;0.7;1" begin="0.7s" dur="0.6s" fill="freeze"/>
      <g>
        <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="rotate" values="-144;0" begin="0.7s" dur="0.6s" fill="freeze"/>
        <path transform="translate(-49250 0)" d="M41750 0l13568-4408-8386 11541V-7133l8386 11541z"/>
      </g>
    </g>
  </g>
</g>
```

The mask circle is stroked, but it is inside the mask, so no stroke shows on the crescent. The `<set>` removes the mask when the sweep ends, because a mask left in place softens the crescent's edges.

## Checking a drawing

Before you finish, compare against the vector:

- Both path `d` strings are byte-for-byte the ones above (or the shapes come from the asset files).
- At most one uniform `scale` on the shared group, no `skew`, no non-uniform scale.
- No `stroke` and no `fill-rule="evenodd"` on the white shapes.
- Red is `#DC0D15` (upper or lower case).
- Render it on red and look: the star's left tip points into the crescent's opening, and the tips are sharp.

# Construction sheet

The flag's shape is set by the table attached to the Turkish Flag Law, Law No. 2893 (Türk Bayrağı Kanunu, accepted 22/9/1983, Resmî Gazete 24/9/1983, no. 18171). Article 10 repeals the earlier flag law, No. 2994 of 29 May 1936. Article 2: the Turkish flag is the white crescent-and-star red flag, in the shapes and proportions shown in the attached table. The table's note: whatever the flag's width, the G ratios don't change.

Details are in the Türk Bayrağı Tüzüğü (No. 85/9034), called "the regulation" here. KHK 700 changed the law's word "tüzük" to "yönetmelik" in 2018, and a transitional article keeps existing tüzükler in force until they're repealed. I found no replacement yönetmelik, so this skill uses the Tüzük.

The official drawing and table: [official-table.png](official-table.png). Translated, with letters as in the law and each value in vector units where G = 60000:

| Letter | Official text | Meaning | Value | Vector units |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G | Genişlik | Width of the flag (height along the pole) | G | 60000 |
| A | Ayın dış çemberi merkezinin uçkurlurluktan [sic] uzaklığı | Distance from the hem to the centre of the outer crescent circle | 1/2 G | 30000 |
| B | Ayın dış çemberinin çapı | Diameter of the outer crescent circle | 1/2 G | 30000 (r 15000) |
| C | Ayın iç ve dış çemberlerinin merkezleri arasındaki uzaklık | Distance between the centres of the inner and outer crescent circles | 0.0625 G | 3750 |
| D | Ayın iç çemberinin çapı | Diameter of the inner crescent circle | 0.4 G | 24000 (r 12000) |
| E | Yıldız çemberinin ayın iç çemberinin uçkurluk yönünde ekseni kestiği noktaya uzaklığı | Distance from the star's circle to the point where the inner crescent circle crosses the centre line on the hem side | 1/3 G | 20000 |
| F | Yıldız çemberinin çapı | Diameter of the star's circle | 1/4 G | 15000 (r 7500) |
| L | Boy | Length of the flag | 1 1/2 G | 90000 |
| M | Uçkurluk genişliği | Width of the hem (the white sleeve at the pole) | 1/30 G | 2000 |

## How the vector follows from it

- Outer circle: centre (30000, 0), radius 15000.
- Inner circle: centre (33750, 0), radius 12000.
- The circles meet at (42675, ±8021), rounded to whole units. Check: 12675² + 8021² ≈ 15000² and 8925² + 8021² ≈ 12000².
- E runs from the inner circle's hem-side crossing of the centre line (33750 - 12000 = 21750) to the star's circle (49250 - 7500 = 41750): 20000 = G/3.
- Star circle: centre (49250, 0), radius 7500. One point at (41750, 0) aims at the crescent. The others sit at 72° steps: (46932, ±7133) and (55318, ±4408).
- The star is a regular five-pointed star whose points lie on that circle.

## The star's position

The official texts disagree slightly, and no drawing can satisfy both rules.

- E = G/3: the law's table and Article 4(G) of the regulation both give this number. It puts the star's tip at x = 41750.
- Article 4(G) of the regulation also says the tip lies where the centre line meets the line through the crescent's two tips, and the official drawing shows it there. With the table's numbers, that line is at x = 42675.

The two differ by 925 units, about 1.5% of G, and no text says which one wins. This skill follows E = G/3, which is a judgement: it's the stated number in both texts, and the Ministry of National Education's flag pattern guide measures the star this way, from the inner circle's crossing of the centre line. The drawing isn't to scale, and the regulation's size chart has no E column, so neither settles it.

## The white hem

M is the white sleeve (uçkurluk) at the pole, marked BEYAZ next to the red (AL) field in the official drawing. A is measured from the hem's inner edge, so the vector's x = 0 is the seam between hem and red.

Article 2 of the regulation measures the length L from the hem's outer edge to the fly, so L includes the hem. When you need the physical flag's full layout, draw the white hem from x = -2000 to 0, and end the red at x = 88000. The total length stays 90000.

The vector in this skill leaves the hem out for screen use. Its red runs from x = 0 to 90000 to keep the 3:2 shape.

## Colour

Law No. 2893 says "al" (red) and "beyaz" (white) and gives no colour code. Article 3(B) of the regulation (Türk Bayrağı Tüzüğü, as amended 17/7/1995) defines them for cloth:

- Red: lightness 27.5, red-green 44.8, yellow-blue 15.6, with a difference of at most 3 NBS.
- White: twice the reflectance at 460 nm minus the reflectance at 620 nm must be at least 15% for silk and synthetic blends, and at least 60% for other cloth.

The regulation doesn't name the colour scale or the illuminant, so these values have no single exact screen equivalent. Read as CIELAB or Hunter Lab, they convert to a much darker red, roughly `#7F152C` to `#9C1411`. Those are my conversions, not official values. Fabric details are left to a mandatory Turkish Standard, which the regulation doesn't number.

For screens use `#DC0D15`, with white `#FFFFFF`. This is a convention. I found no government source that defines a screen colour for the flag itself, though the Turkish Standard wasn't available to read. `#DC0D15` comes from the Interior Ministry, in two places:

- Its [corporate identity page](https://www.icisleri.gov.tr/kurumsal-kimlik-kilavuz) says its logo uses one colour: "Logoda tek renk, bayrak kırmızısı uygulanmıştır."
- Its [2026 corporate identity guide](https://www.icisleri.gov.tr/kurumlar/icisleri.gov.tr/icerikYonetimi/kurumsal-kimlik/icisleri_bakanligi_kurumsal_kimlik_final_2026.pdf), page 55, lists its main corporate red ("Kurumsal Ana Renk") as `#dc0d15`, Pantone 199 C.

Neither place states both facts, so linking them is an inference, and this is a government identity colour, not a rule about the flag. The [Labour Ministry's guide](https://www.csgb.gov.tr/Media/klghey0a/csgb-kurumsal-kimlik.pdf) lists the same hex. The guide also lists RGB 218 41 28, which is `#DA291C` and doesn't match; this skill uses the hex because it's the value that repeats. The ministry's [2018 guide](https://www.icisleri.gov.tr/kurumlar/icisleri.gov.tr/icisleri/Kurumsal/icisleribakanligi_kurumsalkimlik.pdf) does state both facts, flag red and R 227 G 6 B 19 (`#E30613`), Pantone 185 C, but its current page no longer links that guide. If you need the legal colour, for cloth, use the regulation's coordinates.
